memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Make linen undergarments as a covering for the body, reaching from the waist to the thigh. Aaron and his sons must wear them whenever they enter the tent of meeting or approach the altar to minister in the Holy Place, so that they will not incur guilt and die. This is to be a lasting ordinance for Aaron and his descendants." - Exodus 28:42-43 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter ends with the least glamorous garment of all — plain linen undergarments, worn beneath everything else where no one would see them. Yet God commands them explicitly, and attaches serious weight to wearing them. Even what was hidden mattered when approaching God.

There is a thread running from Eden through this verse. When Adam and Eve sinned, they discovered their nakedness and tried to cover themselves, and God made garments for them (Gen 3:21). Covering has always been part of how God deals with human shame in His presence. He does not leave His people exposed; He clothes them.

And He still does. The covering we need before a holy God is not fabric but righteousness, and it is not something we produce. Isaiah confessed that all our righteous acts are like filthy rags (Isa 64:6) — our own coverings are inadequate. But God clothes us in the righteousness of Christ, covering what we could never cover ourselves. Nothing about you needs to be exposed before God, because He Himself has provided what covers you completely.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I trying to cover my own shame rather than receiving the covering God provides?
Does it comfort me that God clothes His people rather than leaving them exposed?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, from Eden until now You have clothed Your people rather than leaving them exposed. Thank You for covering me in the righteousness of Christ. I rest in what You provide. Amen.
